title: 46 years old, $4.3M net worth, and I think I’m finally ready to step away from the market
author: Visible_Driver2308
selftext:
I’m 46 years old, and after 18 years of investing, my net worth has reached around $4.3 million. Recently, I made the decision to step away from active trading through my brokerage accounts and move into a different phase of life.

My portfolio has always been a mix of long-term conviction and selective opportunities. My biggest holdings include companies like NVDA, Tesla, AAPL, GOOG, AMD,MU, along with a small allocation to crypto. I’ve never believed in chasing every hot stock — I prefer owning businesses I believe can continue growing over many years.

For those who are interested in my approach, my stock selection was mostly based on technical structure combined with trend confirmation. I focused on three main setups: ascending triangle breakouts with volume confirmation, double tops/bottoms with neckline timing filters, and flag patterns during ATR volatility compression. I also used multiple moving averages (5/13/34/55-day) to confirm trend strength. When looking for entries, I usually waited for price action to return to my levels rather than chasing breakouts. Sometimes the best trade was simply having the patience not to enter.

Looking back, the biggest lesson wasn’t finding the perfect stock or perfect entry. It was learning how to control emotions, protect capital, and understand that missing an opportunity is always better than forcing a bad trade. I made plenty of mistakes over the years — bought too early, sold too soon, and spent far too much time watching charts.

The funny thing is, reaching this point made me realize something: the market gave me financial freedom, but it also took a lot of my time. There were family trips I postponed, weekends I spent staring at charts, and moments I missed because I was too focused on the next trade.

Now I want to enjoy the things I ignored for years. Spend more time with my wife, travel without checking market movements every few hours, maybe find a quiet place where we can grow flowers, plant vegetables, and enjoy a slower pace of life.

I’m not sure if my experience can help anyone here, but if someone younger reads this, my advice would be simple: build wealth, but don’t forget to build a life along the way.
